stories.name: Vanguard Growth ETF Debate
stories.blurb: A recurring theme of financial articles comparing and recommending Vanguard growth-focused ETFs (like VUG and VGT) against rivals as long-term investment options.

stories.name: Apple iPhone Duo launch
stories.blurb: Apple has unveiled its first foldable smartphone, the $1,999 iPhone Duo, marking its most expensive and dramatically redesigned iPhone yet.

stories.name: iPhone 18 production cuts
stories.blurb: Apple is cutting iPhone 18 Pro component orders and facing rising memory costs, pressuring its stock and pricing power.

stories.name: Apple product launches
stories.blurb: A rolling series of Apple announcements, product releases, and demand signals spanning new iPhones, smart home devices, a leasing program, and expanded U.S. manufacturing.

stories.name: Apple OpenAI trade secrets fight
stories.blurb: Apple and OpenAI are locked in an escalating legal battle over allegations that OpenAI stole Apple trade secrets and confidential files related to unreleased AI devices.

stories.name: Apple CEO transition
stories.blurb: John Ternus succeeds Tim Cook as Apple CEO, raising questions about the company's future direction and leadership style.

stories.name: Apple Q3 earnings preview
stories.blurb: A cluster of headlines previewing Apple's upcoming third-quarter earnings report and debating whether the stock's record highs and rich valuation can be justified by results.

stories.name: Meta's Muse AI Surge
stories.blurb: Meta's stock rallies as its new AI app Muse gains rapid popularity, boosting investor confidence in the company's AI strategy ahead of Meta Connect.

stories.name: TSMC AI chip boom
stories.blurb: TSMC's surging AI chip demand and 2nm progress are driving record revenue and lifting Nvidia and other supplier stocks.

stories.name: Apple Smart Home Push
stories.blurb: Apple is launching a new lineup of smart home devices, led by a $299 HomeView hub with Apple Intelligence and facial recognition, as it challenges Amazon and bets on subscriptions to drive growth.

past.name: Tokenized Stock Trading
past.blurb: Major financial and crypto firms are launching blockchain-based tokens of Apple, Nvidia, Tesla, and other U.S. stocks on Solana and other platforms, enabling 24/7 onchain trading of tokenized equities

past.name: Apple Broadcom chip deal
past.blurb: Apple has signed a multi-year, $30 billion-plus agreement with Broadcom to supply chips through 2031, boosting Broadcom's stock and expanding its Colorado plant.

past.name: Qualcomm Apple patent deal
past.blurb: Qualcomm and Apple renewed their long-term global patent licensing agreement, easing investor fears about Qualcomm's revenue but leaving questions about its growth beyond Apple.

past.name: Iran-Israel Oil Market Swings
past.blurb: Stock markets fluctuate as investors react to escalating and de-escalating US-Iran/Middle East tensions, oil price swings, and their effects on earnings, Fed policy, and economic data.

past.name: Memory Chip Shortage
past.blurb: A global surge in memory and storage chip prices is forcing Apple to raise prices on MacBooks and iPads while even considering banned Chinese chip suppliers to cope with the shortage.

5.text: Apple appears only as one of five mega-cap tech stocks now making up 30.8% of VOO and 49.2% of VUG, cited as concentration risk; the other articles discuss ETF performance and recommendations without substantive Apple developments.

8.text: Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the $1,999–$2,000 Duo, went on sale Friday with limited supplies and sold out quickly in the US and China despite long delays. Apple reportedly asked suppliers to raise production orders by 30%, and its stock hit a record high.

14.text: Loop Capital cut Apple's price target to $330 with a Hold rating, and Jefferies cited shorter delivery times and order cuts as signs of slowing iPhone 18 Pro demand. Morgan Stanley expects holiday-quarter iPhone revenue slightly below estimates, while Cirrus Logic faces iPhone supply-chain pressure.

18.text: Apple’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, launched in stores with strong early demand, 91-day waits, limited pickup stock, and a production ramp despite hinge-related screen failures. IDC kept its 7 million shipment forecast, while iPhone 18 demand disappointed.

6.text: Apple expanded Siri AI to five more languages, launched an OLED iPad mini and M6 iMac, and added AI features to Creator Studio. Other items cover an Apple TV Instagram app, a new home gadget, and Kazakhstan seeking Apple and Google's help enforcing crypto injunctions.

15.text: Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO after 15 years, with John Ternus succeeding him in September 2026. Articles detail each CEO's Apple stock ownership and note Apple's market cap grew from $350 billion to $4.6 trillion under Cook.

7.text: Apple is expected to report Q4 earnings on November 2, with consensus estimates of $2.00 EPS and $112.95 billion revenue, up 8.1% and 10.2% year over year. Articles debate whether the stock, up roughly 27% this year near a $5 trillion market cap, is overvalued or has further upside.

11.text: Meta missed Q3 earnings expectations, though analysts raised targets while flagging elevated 2027 capex and Muse concerns. Its recent capital raise was five times oversubscribed. Apple is not mentioned; the story bears on it only as AI-sector context.

17.text: TSMC is raising prices up to 20% for advanced chip packaging amid AI-driven capacity constraints, and reported a strong Q3 with raised guidance and a Strong Buy rating. The articles barely mention Apple, though TSMC remains its key chip supplier.

19.text: Apple launched a $299 HomeView device plus premium security cameras and accessories, though analysts doubt consumers will pay well above competitors' prices. The articles otherwise barely mention Apple, bearing on it only as scrutiny of its smart home pricing strategy.
